newsitem.title: USA: PSA calls for U.S. bond market regulatory changes.
newsitem.headline: PSA calls for U.S. bond market regulatory changes.

text.p: Securities laws and regulatory procedures should be modified and ammended to maintain transparency, depth and liquidity in the global capital markets, the Public Securities Association (PSA) said in a report on Monday.

Commenting specifically on the Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC) new company registration concept release, "Securities Act Concepts and their Ethics on Capital Formation," PSA said regulatory changes are needed to provide more information to investors.
"Regulators should adopt a number of changes in selected areas of the rules governing primary market offerings and disclosure to investors in both primary and secondary markets," PSA said.
PSA cautioned against adopting at this time the company registration system proposed by the SEC, however, saying it should be "the subject of further evaluation and debate."
PSA said it wants to ensure that the SEC's proposal "would not have a negative impact on the capital formation process and the trading markets."
Among other proposed changes, PSA recommended the following:
* lower threshold definition of qualified institutional investors whom 144A-registered securities underwriters are permitted to solicit
* all investors should receive physical or electronic delivery of transaction-specific information at the time of a new offering of debt securities

* address the needs of MBS/ABS investors who increasingly require a brief description of the economic structure of a transaction and the underlying collateral before the final prospectus is distributed
* all MBS/ABS transaction documents report a minimum set of information to investors at least as frequently, or shortly after each payment date
